introduction: Registering a Will in Tamil Nadu is a straightforward process that ensures your asset distribution is legally recorded. While not mandatory (an unregistered Will is also valid), registration is highly recommended to prove authenticity and avoid future family disputes.
quickFacts:
Important to Know
  • Cost: Approximately ₹500 – ₹1,000 total (includes ₹100 Registration Fee + computer/scanning charges). No Stamp Duty is required.
  • Location: You can register a Will at any Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) in Tamil Nadu. It does not have to be where your property is located, though doing it near your residence is convenient.
  • Time Limit: There is no deadline. You can register a Will at any time during your life.
  • Mandatory Presence: The Testator (person making the Will) and 2 witnesses must physically visit the office.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required for Will Registration

Note: Carry the original documents and one set of photocopies during your visit.
For the Testator (Will Maker)
  • The Will: Original document (can be handwritten or typed on plain paper or bond paper).
  • ID & Address Proof: Aadhaar Card, Passport, Voter ID, or Driving License.
  • Photos: Passport-sized photo.
  • Medical Certificate (Highly Recommended): A certificate from a doctor stating the Testator is of "sound mind," especially if elderly (above 60-65), to prevent claims of pressure or dementia.
For the Two Witnesses
  • ID & Address Proof: Aadhaar Card or other valid ID for both witnesses.
  • Photos: Passport-sized photos of both witnesses.
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Token Booking (TNREGINET)

Important: You cannot complete the full registration online, but you must book an appointment (token) online before visiting the office.
Step-by-Step Token Booking:
  1. Visit Portal: Go to the official TNREGINET website.
  2. User Registration: Click on "Registration" -> "User Registration" to create a free account if you don't have one, and log in.
  3. Create Application: Navigate to "Encumbrance" or "Registration" tab (look for "Create Document" or "Draft"). Select the document type as "Will". Enter the details of the Testator and the Witnesses. You do not need to type the entire content of your Will online, but you must enter the party details to generate the application.
  4. Book Appointment: Once details are saved, click on "Token Booking". Select your preferred Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) and choose a Date and Time slot.
  5. Print Acknowledgement: Download and print the Appointment/Token slip. This is required to enter the SRO office.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Physical Registration at SRO

Note: The Registrar does not read your Will or verify the property details; they only verify your identity and confirm that you are signing it voluntarily.
On the Day of your Appointment:
  1. Arrive Early: Reach the Sub-Registrar Office 15 minutes before your slot with all documents and your 2 witnesses.
  2. Verification: The officer will call your token number. Submit the original Will and the token slip.
  3. Biometrics & Signatures:
    • Testator: Sign the register, provide a thumb impression, and have a digital photo taken.
    • Witnesses: Both witnesses must sign the register, provide their thumb impressions, and show ID proofs.
  4. Scanning: The original Will is scanned into the government system.
  5. Pay Fees: Pay the registration fee (approx ₹100) and scanning charges (approx ₹50-100) at the counter.
afterApplying:
Post-Registration & Options

Will Collection

The original Will is returned to you immediately or within a few hours after scanning. The back of the Will will bear a "Registered" seal with a unique number, date, and the Registrar's signature.

Sealed Cover (Optional Secrecy)

If you want total secrecy, you can opt for a "Deposit of Will" instead of open registration. Place the Will in a sealed envelope and deposit it with the District Registrar. It is kept in a fire-proof safe and only opened after death. This costs slightly more (approx ₹1,000 for deposit).
